html:
My ranking and the official ranking are worlds apart.

Xuan Huang comes first. Ever since he won me over, everything he sings sounds great and full of character; whatever song he takes on, his arrangement makes it his own. Versatile, deeply emotional, with top-class command of the stage: isn’t that exactly the kind of singer a show like this is supposed to find?

Hanggai, the Mongolian folk-rock band, were solid and unspectacular, but still better than everyone else, even if I find their singing a bit boring.

Faouzia spent the whole song being chased by the rhythm; she never really got on top of it. But her pitch is superb and she showed off every trick in the book. Her singing has always been technically top-class and emotionally thin, but that has become a style of its own: she can turn any song into hers with her runs.

Chanté Moore struggled to reach the notes in the second half, with several pitchy moments in the middle. It was nothing like her “If I Ain’t Got You” in the first episode.

Silence Wang was solid, I suppose. A few off-pitch notes are normal enough, and the song doesn’t have much shape anyway. The arrangement was bland too, but the performance was reasonably complete.

Ying Na’s chorus was fine, but she wobbled through every verse. Her breath support wasn’t there, and her pitch and timing were shaky too. The first few performances were easy on the ear, but when she came on I wanted to fast-forward. Add her old-school vocal style, and she just can’t handle a song that’s even slightly up-tempo.

Nan Sun. As a kid I actually liked his songs; I just didn’t like his live singing, because I always felt he wasn’t singing properly. Later I learned he is never in time. He rushes, he drags, and yet by the end of each line he finds his way back, which takes some nerve. But it sounds awful. He sings with so much swagger that the listener can’t get into the song at all; it really grates. People online say there’s nothing wrong with his voice, which is bright and clear, and I didn’t hear him go off pitch either. But could it be that he simply can’t sing in time, not even for a single line…
